To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Event-by-event analysis has been successfully applied to central nuclear collisions, 2) The analysis has been extended from flow to jet studies, 3) The jet studies show that jets are produced in a way that is consistent with perturbative QED and 4) the flow studies show that the final state is consistent with an equilibrated system

(a) the multiparticle correlations of the Pb-Pb system are compatible with the assumption of a thermalized system, and that (b) the multiparticle fluctuations in Pb-Pb collisions can be understood in the context of the statistical bootstrap model.

(i) the event-by-event fluctuations in the azimuthal distributions of charged hadrons are larger in Pb-Pb than in p-p collisions at 158 GeV/c beam momentum, (ii) these event-by-event fluctuations are correlated with the event-by-event multiplicity fluctuations, and (iii) the fluctuations are correlated with flow, i.e. the event-by-event anisotropy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for and study of the manifestations of the underlying dynamics in the multiparticle production process.
the study of the evolution of the nuclear system in heavy-ion collisions.
the following aspects: 1) Event-by-event fluctuations in particle multiplicities, transverse momentum spectra, and flow parameters in Pb-Pb collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon, as measured by NA49.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the jet and flow phenomena have been observed in heavy ion reactions.
jets are a perturbative probe of the initial conditions of a nuclear collision and flow is a hadronic probe of the final state.
jets and flow are the most important and interesting observables in nuclear collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flow of Pb-Pb collisions is a strong function of the initial state.
the observed flow is consistent with the hydrodynamical picture, and that the observed jet-like features are consistent with perturbative QGP.

we have demonstrated that event-by-event fluctuations in Pb-Pb collisions at 158 GeV/c per nucleon are large enough to be observable, but that the signal-to-background ratio is still insufficient to allow for a quantitative analysis with present-day statistics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the event-by-event fluctuations are not only a source of systematic error in the determination of the mean values of flow coefficients, but they can also provide valuable information on the dynamics of the system.
jet and flow observables, while distinct in origin, are also distinct in their event-by-event behavior.
